text.p: Mike Tyson apologized Monday for biting the ears of World Boxing Association champion Evander Holyfield in their title fight Saturday night.

"I apologize to the world, my family and the Nevada State Athletic Commission," Tyson said at a news conference at the MGM Grand casino hotel where two days earlier he was disqualified three rounds into his title rematch with Holyfield.

"I just snapped." Tyson faces a hearing Tuesday by the state commission to consider possible punishment for his actions, which drew worldwide condemnation including from a "horrified: U.S. President Bill Clinton.

"I was wrong and expect to pay the price like a man and I expect the Nevada state athletic commission to hand down a severe penalty and I am here to say I will not fight it," Tyson said. "I only ask that it's not a penalty for life."
Tyson read a prepared statement and took no questions. He had previously said he had to "retaliate" as he did because Holyfield was head-butting him and the referee was doing nothing about it.

"I cannot tell why exactly I acted like I did other than to say when the butting occurred and I thought I might lose because of the cut above my eye, I just snapped and reacted the way many athletes have done and paid the price for it."
Tyson was suspended and his $30 million purse held pending a commission decision. The five-member panel must give Tyson up to 30 days to present his side of things before taking any action.
